| | Happy Disability Pride Month, Friend.

On this day 36 years ago, the Americans with Disabilities Act was signed into law, affirming the dignity of every American, regardless of their ability.

This country was founded on the promise that all of us are created equal – and the disabilities rights movement, with roots right here in Berkeley, fought to enshrine that premise into law.

As the first member of Congress born legally blind, I know firsthand the life-changing power of accessible public services, transportation, and opportunities for work.

That perspective informs my work in Congress and fuels my fight to uphold our shared values.

Earlier this month, I **_[demanded answers from the Department of Labor](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136018461/636087420/-2043926504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTJiMmY1NGItZmE4OC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=c1yFQxO8gGJRhQfLFMWf5-joW0csehhUxIhDbkHT0Ho=&emci=768fe017-ae88-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=52b2f54b-fa88-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=22554739)_** on their failure to protect federal workers with disabilities.

So long as this Administration continues to fail disabled workers, I’ll be there with a spotlight to hold them accountable.

But this fight is about more than one letter. There are two lessons I want to emphasize today.

**1) Much of the disability rights movement was born right here in Berkeley.**

In the late 1960’s and 70’s, a group of UC Berkeley students, led by Ed Roberts and John Hessler, fought for inclusion and accessibility, both on campus and throughout Berkeley.

When the city of Berkeley refused to build curb cuts for wheelchair access, students poured their own concrete ramps overnight until the city conceded.

That victory laid the foundation for section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, which later paved the way for the ADA itself.

Today, Ed’s legacy is enshrined in sidewalks and campuses across the nation, as well as the Ed Roberts Campus adjacent to the Ashby BART Station, which hosts the Center for Independent Living and other organizations fighting for Ed’s vision.

**2) When we prioritize accessibility, everyone benefits - that’s why the disability community is at the center of my work.**

In Washington, I’ve championed efforts to expand access and protect disability rights. From fighting to modernize para-transit services to match the realities of modern life to ensuring small businesses are accessible for workers.

**When we design systems and places that welcome _anyone_ , we make those spaces more appealing for _everyone_.**

So happy Disability Pride Month.

Take a moment today to appreciate the disabled advocates who fought to get us this far.

Then tomorrow, let’s get back in the fight. We still have a world to build that works for everyone.

In solidarity,

Lateefah

| Hi, it’s Dan Osborn, the Independent candidate running to defeat Republican Billionaire Pete Ricketts for U.S. Senate in Nebraska.

I’m going to level with you.

My team and I are sitting down right now to make tough calls about this campaign that could decide whether we win or lose.

→ How many people can we afford to put on the ground?
→ How many doors can we knock?
→ How loud can we make our message when we’re up against someone with unlimited money?

Because here’s what I’m up against:**_My opponent is a billionaire. I’m not._**

I don’t have a pile of cash to fall back on. I don’t have corporate PACs waiting in line to bail me out. What I’ve got is a campaign built the hard way — by regular people chipping in what they can.

**_And right now, we’ve got gaps to close. If we don’t start raising more money, we’ll have to make tough decisions about which outreach programs to keep and which to cut._**

[So I’m asking straight up: Can you pitch in $10 or whatever you can right now to the Voter Protection Project and my campaign so we can keep building this campaign?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/120733?t=6&akid=26929%2E878179%2EJzdGgM) | [DONATE »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/120733?t=7&akid=26929%2E878179%2EJzdGgM)
---
Every dollar we raise goes directly into reaching more people — more conversations, more momentum, more chances to prove that this race doesn’t belong to the highest bidder.

I won’t pretend this part is fun. Asking for money never is.

But I believe in what we’re building here. And I believe that if enough regular folks step up, we can beat someone who thinks this seat can be bought.
****
[So I’ll ask one more time: Will you chip in today to me and the Voter Protection Project to help us close the gap and keep this campaign moving?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/120733?t=8&akid=26929%2E878179%2EJzdGgM)

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: This Ann Richards quote hits home.
body:
Ann Richards energy.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
One of my favorite Ann Richards quotes has always been her line about Ginger Rogers.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260726_1_ann.E6cpKQ&refcode=em20260726-1656&amount=5&t=1&akid=1656%2E299639%2EKiWC8p)
**Working in the Texas Legislature, that line really hits home.**
My Democratic colleagues and I spend _years_ fighting for policies that benefit all Texans.**But without fail, time after time, Republicans block our bills. Then they turn around years later, rebrand those exact same ideas as their own, and take all the credit.**
It’s shameless on their part, but it never brings us down. We don’t stop fighting — we can’t. Because Texas families need us to push through the noise and deliver real results.
That grit and stubborn persistence is what I call true Ann Richards energy. It’s what keeps me going in this campaign for Texas governor every day.
**Right now, all that hard work is paying off. New polling shows our campaign is just 3 points behind Greg Abbott.**
These are true Ann Richards margins, Peter. Taking back Texas and giving our state the leadership it deserves is _finally_ within our reach.
To turn these close polls into a huge win this November, we need to have the resources to make it possible. That’s why we launched a**$100,000 fundraising goal** to make sure we have the resources to travel across Texas and talk to voters face-to-face about the stakes of this race.
**[Peter, will you pitch in $5 today to help us hit our $100,000 fundraising goal by Friday and keep this momentum going all the way to November?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260726_1_ann.E6cpKQ&refcode=em20260726-1656&amount=5&t=2&akid=1656%2E299639%2EKiWC8p)**

Thank you,
Gina

body:
This goes far beyond politics. The fabric of America is unweaving.

| | | | | A Personal Message From Mike
---
Friend,
---
I am reaching out to you directly because, quite frankly, I don't know where else to turn. I've spent the last few hours pacing the room, trying to process what is happening. The latest developments are incredibly daunting, and my heart is heavy with an overwhelming sense of urgency.

name: Wes Moore
subject: An act of hope
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1664%2E1086043%2ElJU1sB)
Peter, I don’t come from a political background. This is the first political office I ever held.
When I ran for office the first time a few years ago, I had to convince many of my family members to vote for me. It’s not like we aren’t cool. They just don’t rush to the ballot box every year.
**It struck me that people I love -- people who cared deeply about their communities and their country -- had been absent from a democratic act that generations of Americans fought for.**
Somewhere along the way, they stopped believing that politics had much to do with them -- or that anyone in politics had much interest in them.
That realization has stayed with me. And it is exactly why I value our democracy so much.
Democracy is a relationship. Those who have the privilege of serving in government share a responsibility to give people a reason to believe their participation counts. To earn their trust. To show the public that government is not something that happens to us, but something we have the power to shape.
As an elected official, I take that responsibility seriously. It’s sacred, and essential.
If those of us in public office do our jobs right, then voting becomes about more than casting a ballot. It is an act of hope.
**[It’s with that continued hope that I’m running for re-election, and I hope that you’re with me in that mission. Will you chip in to power our campaign today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260726-1.BV4mzE&refcode=em-20260726-1&t=2&akid=1664%2E1086043%2ElJU1sB)**

Thank you, Peter.

A bombshell
report reveals Chief Justice John Roberts helped build the Supreme Court’s
“shadow docket” — a backdoor process for major rulings with no full
briefing, no arguments, and often no explanation.

What started as a rarely used emergency tool has been transformed into a
quiet pipeline for reshaping the law out of public view.

And under Trump, it’s been weaponized.

When Trump gets blocked in lower courts for breaking the law or pushing
unconstitutional policies, he runs straight to the Supreme Court demanding
an “emergency” order.

And this Court delivers:

30+ requests.
~80% success rate.

These are supposed to be temporary rulings. They’re not.

Immigrants lose protections. Civil servants get pushed out. Limits on
presidential power disappear all through unsigned, late-night orders with
no explanation.

Roberts set this precedent. Now it’s the playbook.

The bottom line is: this Court is operating without transparency,
accountability, or the restraint our democracy demands — and it won’t
change on its own.

Demand Justice PAC is exposing these abuses and building public and
political pressure needed to force reform — from ethics rules to
structural changes that rein in this out-of-control Court. But that
pressure only works if we can scale it.

Long before I ran for Congress, I had the opportunity to serve as policy director for Barack Obama’s 2004 campaign for the United States Senate.
That campaign taught me something I have carried with me ever since:
Winning takes more than a good candidate.
It takes a clear message. A strong organization. The resources to compete. And people willing to believe in a campaign before everyone else catches on.
Since then, I have gone on to win five elections of my own and help build coalitions around some of the toughest challenges facing working families.
But I also saw the same problem over and over again.
Too many talented leaders never get the early support they need. Too many important causes struggle for resources while Republicans and their billionaire donors build political infrastructure years in advance.
That is why I founded Equal Opportunity Now.
We are building an organization that can identify bold leaders, invest in them early, and support the causes that will expand opportunity, stand up to Donald Trump’s MAGA agenda, and deliver real results for working families.

Friend,
Growing up in Kansas, we were taught that the Second Amendment isn't just a line in a law book, it’s the ultimate insurance policy for a free people.
It’s about the right to protect your home, your family, and our way of life without asking for permission from a bureaucrat in a far-Left city.
I’ve spent my career fighting to protect the rights of Kansas families, not criminals. But I can’t do this alone.
I’m standing in the breach to stop them, but the Left is relentless. They believe that if they yell loud enough and spend enough money, we’ll eventually fold. But they’ve got another thing coming...
We must show the DC elites a massive wall of opposition from the Heartland. So will you please add your name to our 2A Defense Petition before midnight so they know our nation will NEVER be disarmed?

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. # **DSA teachers Plot to Reshape NYC Schools Around Socialist Curriculum**
Democratic Socialists of America educators held a meeting titled **["Planning for Socialist School Governance,"](https://substack.com/redirect/8cc84b9e-dba3-40a4-b1a2-0d860ab28cdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** calling for NYC public school curricula to be rebuilt around Marxist class consciousness and the teachings of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. CUNY professor Maureen Fadem argued the existing curriculum was built on a "neoliberal and conservative frame" and demanded it be overhauled to include "race consciousness" training for teachers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8cc84b9e-dba3-40a4-b1a2-0d860ab28cdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The group openly discussed exploiting their connections to Mayor Mamdani to advance the agenda.** DSA Labor Working Group co-chair Nina Bruckenthal said the group planned to leverage upcoming United Federation of Teachers contract negotiations -- set to expire in November 2027 -- to embed far-left demands into teacher agreements. One participant warned that unpopular reforms could drive parents toward charter schools, prompting calls to fight school choice.
* **Critics called the effort "grooming,"** with former Community Education Council President Maud Maron warning the group was seeking access to other people's children to convert them to their ideology.

* * *
# **Venezuelan illegal immigrant charged in death of Florida grandmother**
Carlos Suarez-Contreras, 26, a Venezuelan national allegedly in the country illegally, has been **[charged with driving with a canceled license causing death](https://substack.com/redirect/c7b88cc6-52ff-4672-9c7d-78d943ae5f7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after backing his SUV over 82-year-old Deborah Murphy in a Panama City Beach Publix parking lot on May 17.

A van drove **[into a crowd of people celebrating Berlin's Christopher Street Day pride event](https://substack.com/redirect/e87bef99-3d8c-4f77-b121-24c921ed0311?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Saturday night, killing one person and injuring at least 16 others, several critically. The attack occurred around 10 p.m. when the vehicle entered Tiergarten park along the parade route and struck multiple people before hitting a tree. Authorities are also investigating reports that some victims sustained stab wounds in addition to impact injuries.

There are only 100 days left to give our candidates the support they need to win.
#
Peter,
Today marks 100 days until Election Day, and we’re facing our next end-of-month fundraising deadline on July 31.
What we raise before then will help determine how much support we can give the first candidates on Small Town PAC’s 2026 endorsement slate—and how many more competitive races we can invest in before November.
[**I’ll say more about why that matters in a moment. But first, I’m going to get right to it: Can you make a contribution of $5 or whatever makes sense for you to help us hit our July goal?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260726-1.37Tb0P&amount=5&refcode=em20260726-895&t=2&akid=895%2E34582%2EwmmpN5)
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260726-1.37Tb0P&amount=5&refcode=20260726-895&t=21&akid=895%2E34582%2EwmmpN5)**
I started Small Town PAC because too many politicians have treated small towns and rural communities like places to visit in the final weeks of an election instead of communities worth showing up for and investing in.
You don’t rebuild trust by parachuting in with a TV ad. You do it by showing up, listening, and supporting leaders who actually understand the communities they want to represent.
That’s why I’m so proud of the first three candidates on our 2026 endorsement slate.
Jake Johnson is a teacher running for Congress in the Southern Minnesota district I used to represent.
Sarah Trone Garriott is a minister, working mom, and State Senator who has proven she can bring people together and win tough races in Iowa.
Rachel Wallace is a lifelong public servant with deep roots in Pennsylvania who knows how government works—and how it can work better for her community.
These are working-class leaders with fresh ideas and firsthand experience dealing with the problems facing their neighbors. They know what it’s like to worry about the next medical bill, the price at the gas pump, or how much groceries will cost this week.
And most importantly: _they’re running to do something about it._
But earning an endorsement is only the beginning. Now, we have to make sure Jake, Sarah, and Rachel have the support they need to overcome Republican attacks, outside spending, and all the right-wing noise coming their way.
**Every dollar we raise now helps us invest while there is still time to make a difference—before the airwaves are flooded with attack ads and before voters begin making their final decisions.**
The other side has billionaires, tech bros, venture capitalists, and robber barons willing to spend whatever it takes to protect their power.
We have people chipping in a few dollars at a time because they believe working families deserve leaders who know them, listen to them, and will fight for them.

Because in order to have a healthy, sustainable economy, we need Vermont to be the best place for working families. But I want to be very clear — this is not, and cannot, be accomplished at the expense of older Vermonters. They’ve paid their dues and built the state we love, yet many now live on fixed incomes and struggle to afford to live here. So let’s talk about the bookends of life and how we’ll make Vermont a place where everyone’s needs are met. We took a big swing with child care and showed the country what’s possible. The law is working as we had hoped:
* 5,000 more children are receiving child care tuition assistance
* 4,800 families have tuition-free child care
* 1,700 new child care spaces have been created
* Wages for child care workers have increased by 30%
* And for the first time in a decade, the number of home-based child care programs — called family child care homes — is growing.

I’m so proud of these results, but we still have more to do. I’m eager to finish the job by making sure child care is affordable for all families and continuing to support our early childhood educators by ensuring they have the compensation and recognition they deserve. I will also ensure that older Vermonters can stay here in Vermont and age on their own terms. This means...
* putting money back in older Vermonters’ pockets by lowering taxes on Social Security income
* making it easier and more affordable to downsize into turnkey housing options for those who choose to do so
* connecting older Vermonters to the transportation they need, and
* supporting folks who are providing vital care to older family members

The ways in which we care for our youngest and oldest community members say a lot about who we are as a state. As your governor — and as both a mom and daughter myself — I will value caregivers and the wonderful humans in need of their care. We will ensure a strong start for our young ones and well-deserved stability through the later years of life. [**Watch me discuss my approach to ensuring care for Vermonters of all ages — from child care to aging on your own terms.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136030611/636120417/-1345861360?refcode=ea.59471e15-0a89-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.59471e15-0a89-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTk0NzFlMTUtMGE4OS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=bMgIwnod9lwFvUxYNCxLLY3DSyH1JDXhw31HC778rSI=&emci=13ef4473-8e87-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=59471e15-0a89-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378) | [**WATCH**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136030612/636120418/-1345861360?refcode=ea.59471e15-0a89-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.59471e15-0a89-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTk0NzFlMTUtMGE4OS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=bMgIwnod9lwFvUxYNCxLLY3DSyH1JDXhw31HC778rSI=&emci=13ef4473-8e87-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=59471e15-0a89-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378)

Team, we’ll get right to the point.
We’re asking you to make a donation to Mark Kelly and Jacky Rosen.
If that’s all you need to hear, use this link and chip in.
**_[https://secure.actblue.com/contribute/page/rosenfornevada_kelly/5-27-2026](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136032792/636127682/-1087597766?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5852-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMjM5NDZjMi0wYjg5LWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lIIghzYi6VDAUJrFerdHUC51tHsvCiVDnE9pb3-1zas=)_**
If you’d like a little more, would you let us explain? This won’t take long.
Mark retired from the Navy 15 years ago, after Gabby was shot.
He thought his time in public service was over until Donald Trump became president. By 2019, Mark knew he couldn’t sit on the sidelines anymore. He ran for Senate and won his first campaign in 2020. Then he had to turn around and run again for a full term in 2022, and he won that race, too.
And late last year, after a lifetime of service, the Trump Administration came after him.
For speaking the truth and supporting the Constitution, the President of the United States said Mark should be hanged. The Secretary of Defense threatened him with court-martial, censured him, and is trying to reduce his retirement rank and pay.

July 26, 2026

Connecticut is a frustrating state to live in for us political junkies, whether you are a liberal or a conservative. As it is Deep Blue, statewide elections are a foregone conclusion and there hasn't been a Republican Congressman since 2008. Furthermore, the archaic convention system strongly supported by both political parties makes it difficult to primary incumbents while the incomprehensible public financing system of state elections discourages further competition.
But every once in a while, a race comes along that is quite entertaining to follow, and this is now happening in the First Congressional District which encompasses Hartford and its surroundings. The district is so Deep Blue that a random name from the phone book will win the race for the Democrats in November. Thus, the Democratic primary on August 11 is the Big Enchilada.

Presently, the seat is held by the career politician John Larson, who at age seventy-eight has been in Connecticut politics for so long that he once opposed the state income tax. The former East Hartford Mayor has held this seat since 1999.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6de39676-cb10-44cf-b25b-15e092f4c33e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congressman John Larson

Enter Luke Bronin. Born in Rye, New York, Bronin grew up in Greenwich and garnered the necessary credentials to enter America's Ruling Class: Phillips Exeter Academy, Yale, Rhodes Scholarship at Oxford and Yale Law School. He served as an intelligence officer in the US Navy, serving in Afghanistan.

But this talented man also became a law firm partner at a young age while finding the time to produce an album of seven songs, one of which was featured in the television show, Dawson's Creek.

But he became interested in politics and public service, working both in the Obama administration and that of former Connecticut Governor Dan Malloy. He then was elected Mayor of Hartford where his claim to fame was quickly realizing that this city was hopelessly broke and successfully lobbying the legislature to subsidize it, a policy that continues to this day.

Larson, on the other hand, is a meat-and-potatoes Democrat who sees his role as distributing wealth and protecting Social Security. Before Bronin's challenge, Larson thought ICE was the solid state of water, Iran was a type of herbal tea and climate change was caused by fire-breathing dragons.

But as there is virtually no ideological differences between these two, the campaign is getting personal, with Larson accusing Bronin of being a billionaire puppet while Bronin is implying Larson is a fossilized corporate stooge who accepts money from PACs (Political Action Committees). Expect the attacks to become more vicious in the following days.

But the Democrats should stick with Larson as he is a master of constituent service. Several years ago, one of my patients had horrendous glaucoma in one eye that required two surgical procedures and multiple eye drops to preserve his sight. And we were succeeding in doing so.
That is until the VA (Veterans Administration) refused to pay for one of his eye drops. I wrote letters, filled out forms and spent considerable time on hold dealing with listless VA bureaucrats who couldn't care less that this patient, who had honorably served his country, was going to lose the sight in this eye without this medication.

Exasperated, I called John Larson's Congressional office and left a message. Within minutes, a polite and concerned aide returned my call and listened attentively while I pled my patient's case. Several hours later, the patient appeared in my office and informed me the VA had called him and the medication was now covered.

After that, I would have voted for Larson had I lived in his district. And I am a hardcore Republican. His staff saved my patient's sight.

Will Bronin be this responsive? Who knows? But Bronin will be more interested in getting on to CNN an MS NOW and pontificating on foreign policy.

It should be mentioned in all fairness that there are other candidates. State Assemblywoman Jillian Gilchrest is on the ballot. She has made a name for herself a fierce abortion rights (now euphemistically called "reproductive care") advocate and teaches at the so-called Catholic institution, [The University of St. Joseph](https://substack.com/redirect/d4a98465-9aef-44d7-884c-b9f7e1207b92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). My patron saint must be rolling over in his grave. But if elected, she would certainly go to bat for any constituent seeking the abortion inducing drug, mifepristone.
Also in the race is Ruth Fortune who was unfairly initially excluded from the ballot because of the archaic convention system but managed to garner enough signatures to correct this injustice.

But neither Fortune or Gilchrest have raised enough money to be competitive, so unless lightning strikes, Larson or Bronin will win the primary. Stay tuned.

clean_body: But the Democrats Should Stick with John Larson | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more But the Democrats Should Stick with John Larson | | | Jul 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | July 26, 2026 Connecticut is a frustrating state to live in for us political junkies, whether you are a liberal or a conservative. As it is Deep Blue, statewide elections are a foregone conclusion and there hasn't been a Republican Congressman since 2008. Furthermore, the archaic convention system strongly supported by both political parties makes it difficult to primary incumbents while the incomprehensible public financing system of state elections discourages further competition. But every once in a while, a race comes along that is quite entertaining to follow, and this is now happening in the First Congressional District which encompasses Hartford and its surroundings. The district is so Deep Blue that a random name from the phone book will win the race for the Democrats in November. Thus, the Democratic primary on August 11 is the Big Enchilada. Presently, the seat is held by the career politician John Larson, who at age seventy-eight has been in Connecticut politics for so long that he once opposed the state income tax. The former East Hartford Mayor has held this seat since 1999. | | ---|---|--- Congressman John Larson Enter Luke Bronin. Born in Rye, New York, Bronin grew up in Greenwich and garnered the necessary credentials to enter America's Ruling Class: Phillips Exeter Academy, Yale, Rhodes Scholarship at Oxford and Yale Law School. He served as an intelligence officer in the US Navy, serving in Afghanistan. But this talented man also became a law firm partner at a young age while finding the time to produce an album of seven songs, one of which was featured in the television show, Dawson's Creek. But he became interested in politics and public service, working both in the Obama administration and that of former Connecticut Governor Dan Malloy. He then was elected Mayor of Hartford where his claim to fame was quickly realizing that this city was hopelessly broke and successfully lobbying the legislature to subsidize it, a policy that continues to this day. Larson, on the other hand, is a meat-and-potatoes Democrat who sees his role as distributing wealth and protecting Social Security. Before Bronin's challenge, Larson thought ICE was the solid state of water, Iran was a type of herbal tea and climate change was caused by fire-breathing dragons. But as there is virtually no ideological differences between these two, the campaign is getting personal, with Larson accusing Bronin of being a billionaire puppet while Bronin is implying Larson is a fossilized corporate stooge who accepts money from PACs (Political Action Committees). Expect the attacks to become more vicious in the following days. But the Democrats should stick with Larson as he is a master of constituent service. Several years ago, one of my patients had horrendous glaucoma in one eye that required two surgical procedures and multiple eye drops to preserve his sight. And we were succeeding in doing so. That is until the VA (Veterans Administration) refused to pay for one of his eye drops. I wrote letters, filled out forms and spent considerable time on hold dealing with listless VA bureaucrats who couldn't care less that this patient, who had honorably served his country, was going to lose the sight in this eye without this medication. Exasperated, I called John Larson's Congressional office and left a message. Within minutes, a polite and concerned aide returned my call and listened attentively while I pled my patient's case. Several hours later, the patient appeared in my office and informed me the VA had called him and the medication was now covered. After that, I would have voted for Larson had I lived in his district. And I am a hardcore Republican. His staff saved my patient's sight. Will Bronin be this responsive? Who knows? But Bronin will be more interested in getting on to CNN an MS NOW and pontificating on foreign policy. It should be mentioned in all fairness that there are other candidates. State Assemblywoman Jillian Gilchrest is on the ballot. She has made a name for herself a fierce abortion rights (now euphemistically called "reproductive care") advocate and teaches at the so-called Catholic institution, . My patron saint must be rolling over in his grave. But if elected, she would certainly go to bat for any constituent seeking the abortion inducing drug, mifepristone. Also in the race is Ruth Fortune who was unfairly initially excluded from the ballot because of the archaic convention system but managed to garner enough signatures to correct this injustice. But neither Fortune or Gilchrest have raised enough money to be competitive, so unless lightning strikes, Larson or Bronin will win the primary. Stay tuned. | | | Dear 7 Directions of Service Members, Friends, Allies and Partners, We are excited to invite you to join us for a special two-night gathering bringing together film, environmental justice, Indigenous leadership, and community action. [RSVP here:](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_FT7Gu-Afu4SfCQt89-9sxVnTGzwVd-ZDv07eCTtUt_z4St821TKUTVmWarFzpTwP8LTzzYHgOtxUEAnCc8UoLvm_9PK2eF3ajR36fguiIDu4jk7re8b9lXYn2jYkCz2AfdKmTOuowFM0fxdaEefG_XWhvuxWPH8D7ighqjtZOqWVhiN4Qh53RrQzucAq6TFBhK_yKm2HS_owMqXAMSwx9BeYND6V6q6k3CFjDGZTtmvwDA3Jfcqp-gc6wwZsHOBJ944s7Gmd0fRMmazAd0INb23vAqKe8S5xP6xD1WT8d1s6JXk2i1ZDhccwvfBkKcCe59J-9iWcRM_e0JsT2mMdAo0wLhoB_l1VVnEpthz5-29khQoVOBB4ZPIBOs3Xt8SiIPAZKrBdD9KrP7JZwkFBpVCCsZz781MEWAMW7oN75D1wiSqV_eBlOEy_eB8eXR9I/4sn/UnDnfUhLREOWyQWi5y1jyQ/h0/h001.AS-Yx-BMGV_8qdY5L28JKjF-Kmoifot7GR4uVCcmrFk) **VS. GOLIATH: Stories from the Frontlines** **August 26–27, 2026**
**Varsity Theatre | Chapel Hill, NC**
**Doors Open: 6:00 PM** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_FT7Gu-Afu4SfCQt89-9sxVnTGzwVd-ZDv07eCTtUt_z4St821TKUTVmWarFzpTwPgiow7Kobu32SprCa6C12-wp7cnmLnuVwHsFs0g9ckLlpABQkqClXUow6q4ctq54NdsXTMzYfQwzRVVH96tTy6OHsupkiZjgqVhq7jddNbTX575zyM1fUZy9MDgM7uWHTxAgejytJhyyE76zuxXmqBY4qlt35lTDa3rb9lnN5ofIq0H9XkJPM4X8HnbOqYQXtt5sfimsZw32BDezTQTptooZ4QrOza-fkBUo9Gy5q2RPqSa2QPGhtcrTGyUqhPRdSQnFDZ77hbBNrHXi3eSVG7VrGqW8FZdttJR7VLra1hDs3w-ffC1ay65PLWuj9Z_5Dm6faLP4XkthXhx0hU6QgCaatFbyruUHRXwcRprDfHqkB35WtjD-zVJlhS91d2MC0/4sn/UnDnfUhLREOWyQWi5y1jyQ/h1/h001.9HuslgUAP-84_jeK7yeMRg_lIXVeNVH8nb0iGVnyqLk)**** For the past several years, many of you have stood alongside 7 Directions of Service as we have worked to protect our water, land, sacred places, communities, and future. This gathering is an opportunity to see our struggles within a much larger story—and to learn from communities across the country who are standing up to powerful industries and refusing to allow their homes to become sacrifice zones.
### What is VS. GOLIATH?
Executive produced by Don Cheadle and The Solutions Project, Fossil Free Media, and The Equation Campaign, **VS. GOLIATH** is an award-winning documentary series from Tikkun Olam Productions. The series takes audiences directly to the frontlines of environmental justice struggles through the stories of people who decided they would not remain silent while corporations threatened their communities. These are stories of resistance, courage, community—and what becomes possible when ordinary people decide to stand against Goliath.
### Wednesday, August 26 — Appalachia & Cancer Alley
**Doors Open: 6:00 PM |** Night One takes us to Appalachia and Louisiana's Cancer Alley. We will hear from veterans, farmers, Indigenous leaders, landowners, faith leaders, and community organizers confronting the Mountain Valley Pipeline, petrochemical development, industrial pollution, and the enormous corporate and political forces behind them. Their struggles raise questions that are deeply familiar to us here in North Carolina: What happens when communities are told that pollution and sacrifice are simply the price of development? And what happens when those communities say **no**?
### Thursday, August 27 — Greater Chaco Region
**Doors Open: 6:00 PM |** Night Two centers Indigenous leadership and the Greater Chaco region—a living cultural landscape of profound significance to Indigenous peoples that has faced decades of pressure from oil and gas development. This story asks a fundamental question: **What happens when places Indigenous peoples consider sacred are treated simply as resources to be extracted?** That question reaches all the way back to our own communities. Across North Carolina, Indigenous peoples, landowners, environmental advocates, and allies are confronting pipelines and development projects that threaten waterways, ancestral landscapes, archaeological sites, cultural resources, and potential burial grounds. We are being forced to ask: **Who decides what is sacred?
Whose history is protected?
Who bears the consequences of development?
And what responsibility do we have when the places our ancestors left in our care are threatened?**
### Two Nights. Three Regions. One Shared Struggle.
**Appalachia. Cancer Alley. Greater Chaco.** Different landscapes. Different communities. Different histories. Yet the struggles are connected by questions of corporate power, environmental justice, Indigenous rights, public health, sacred places, and who gets to decide what happens to the land. Environmental justice fights can often feel like David versus Goliath. Corporations may have money, attorneys, lobbyists, consultants, and political influence. But communities have something powerful, too.
* **Community knowledge matters.**
* **Indigenous knowledge matters.**
* **Organizing matters.**
* **Speaking up matters.**
* ******Standing together matters.**

And Goliath does not always win.
### More Than a Film Screening
We don't want you to simply watch these stories. We want you to **witness them, talk about them, connect them to what is happening here at home—and take action.** Following the films, we will create space for community conversation and opportunities to connect with people working on the frontlines of environmental justice in North Carolina. Whether you have been organizing with us for years or are just beginning to learn about these issues, **you belong in this conversation.** We hope our 7DS members will come out, stand with us, and help us fill the Varsity Theatre for these two important nights. **[Bring a friend. Bring a neighbor. Bring your questions. Bring your voice.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3_FT7Gu-Afu4SfCQt89-9sxVnTGzwVd-ZDv07eCTtUt_z4St821TKUTVmWarFzpTwOhe815y20XwNPTsvWddc1ZPmeeEkcH2g-Mrpo3BE8oUGQ6u_QxfDoWAV0DeSPCva0N4XrOAgP3mLx-rPH6x2PhiGSVbwW7inJwBzKaghpMnYAVOB5onMrcXAPjTIeIdl409EyKQhxjdf6oyYVHU2cZHAi-U7yohqFstFHYFkQJPA7sJepeKCPH7zCfjREzNWY6PzATsxGqBm5UkcgBHpsaO8YfE5hyN4cnOSYdg298oTgGtVJKGvpRkIDN8Fk3n8zcsLMXt7Qacs_DAdcjYvuuTn_svGNLMNu-6veSQ_-tENY8qKYvTJK3xSxTscuwYz5745b2sB13ylF0LzF2WfuvS1ru212Nb8ALcDlH6h3DzSGlPR8BEOQEQ8kUj4z84vk/4sn/UnDnfUhLREOWyQWi5y1jyQ/h2/h001.h9LZ6lVqybMNyzAWZlcH9sEasX6cRPvH_zeXzfKHy4E) ** If you would like to **co-sponsor the event on Action Network and share the invitation with your members, supporters, and networks, please let me know.** We would be honored to have your organization standing with us and helping bring more people into this conversation. Please send Crystal an email with your sponsoring group ID on Action Network. We look forward to seeing you there. In solidarity, **Crystal & Jason Crazy Bear****

clean_body: | | | Dear 7 Directions of Service Members, Friends, Allies and Partners, We are excited to invite you to join us for a special two-night gathering bringing together film, environmental justice, Indigenous leadership, and community action. VS. GOLIATH: Stories from the Frontlines August 26–27, 2026 Varsity Theatre | Chapel Hill, NC Doors Open: 6:00 PM ** For the past several years, many of you have stood alongside 7 Directions of Service as we have worked to protect our water, land, sacred places, communities, and future. This gathering is an opportunity to see our struggles within a much larger story—and to learn from communities across the country who are standing up to powerful industries and refusing to allow their homes to become sacrifice zones. What is VS. GOLIATH? Executive produced by Don Cheadle and The Solutions Project, Fossil Free Media, and The Equation Campaign, VS. GOLIATH is an award-winning documentary series from Tikkun Olam Productions. The series takes audiences directly to the frontlines of environmental justice struggles through the stories of people who decided they would not remain silent while corporations threatened their communities. These are stories of resistance, courage, community—and what becomes possible when ordinary people decide to stand against Goliath. Wednesday, August 26 — Appalachia & Cancer Alley Doors Open: 6:00 PM | Night One takes us to Appalachia and Louisiana's Cancer Alley. We will hear from veterans, farmers, Indigenous leaders, landowners, faith leaders, and community organizers confronting the Mountain Valley Pipeline, petrochemical development, industrial pollution, and the enormous corporate and political forces behind them. Their struggles raise questions that are deeply familiar to us here in North Carolina: What happens when communities are told that pollution and sacrifice are simply the price of development? And what happens when those communities say no? Thursday, August 27 — Greater Chaco Region Doors Open: 6:00 PM | Night Two centers Indigenous leadership and the Greater Chaco region—a living cultural landscape of profound significance to Indigenous peoples that has faced decades of pressure from oil and gas development. This story asks a fundamental question: What happens when places Indigenous peoples consider sacred are treated simply as resources to be extracted? That question reaches all the way back to our own communities. Across North Carolina, Indigenous peoples, landowners, environmental advocates, and allies are confronting pipelines and development projects that threaten waterways, ancestral landscapes, archaeological sites, cultural resources, and potential burial grounds. We are being forced to ask: Who decides what is sacred? Whose history is protected? Who bears the consequences of development? And what responsibility do we have when the places our ancestors left in our care are threatened? Two Nights. Three Regions. One Shared Struggle. Appalachia. Cancer Alley. Greater Chaco. Different landscapes. Different communities. Different histories. Yet the struggles are connected by questions of corporate power, environmental justice, Indigenous rights, public health, sacred places, and who gets to decide what happens to the land. Environmental justice fights can often feel like David versus Goliath. Corporations may have money, attorneys, lobbyists, consultants, and political influence. But communities have something powerful, too. Community knowledge matters. Indigenous knowledge matters. Organizing matters. Speaking up matters. ****Standing together matters. And Goliath does not always win. More Than a Film Screening We don't want you to simply watch these stories. We want you to witness them, talk about them, connect them to what is happening here at home—and take action. Following the films, we will create space for community conversation and opportunities to connect with people working on the frontlines of environmental justice in North Carolina. Whether you have been organizing with us for years or are just beginning to learn about these issues, you belong in this conversation. We hope our 7DS members will come out, stand with us, and help us fill the Varsity Theatre for these two important nights. If you would like to co-sponsor the event on Action Network and share the invitation with your members, supporters, and networks, please let me know. We would be honored to have your organization standing with us and helping bring more people into this conversation. Please send Crystal an email with your sponsoring group ID on Action Network. We look forward to seeing you there. clean_body: Trump’s $15 million reflecting-pool mess = Donald Trump wanted a showpiece. Taxpayers got a mess. His plan to “beautify” the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool ballooned from $2 million to $15 million. The paint peeled. The water turned green with algae. And now the same contractor is being brought back to repair its own failed work. = That is money spent on Trump’s whims while American families are trying to afford the basics. I called Donald Trump a “sad, pathetic, lonely man” because no president should get to turn public money into a vanity project — then reward the people who made a mess of it. = I have launched an Oversight Committee investigation because the public deserves to know who approved these contracts, why the costs exploded, and why the same contractor is getting more taxpayer money. No president’s vanity project should become a sweetheart deal. = = Thank you, Robert Garcia = * Paid for by Robert Garcia for Congress Robert Garcia for Congress 65 Pine Ave #348 Long Beach, CA 90802 United States This email was sent to . Fellow Patriot,

After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate.

**President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's _"Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate._**

I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, _**but I am ready.**_

I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge.

It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times.

I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for.

I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot.

But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. **[However, I cannot do this alone.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=34ffe847ec544432b5a554ffb95819e1&_e=0Rf02laGbWzMkIa0ZliwZRqQA3rv2dMAOAIK8CuDs-a-oavBIebTJUzxNGoxBwtrlWuFD65YBNvQFddBpLvx0TJ8IvkDPkJC6nSIQx9DWeGK593fe2yFs3Ec0iNTQA4Jbw0cEnJWUj79OU_HFyORAdOOZptMSzPGt7imc_fCtBWfay44QeTjUn_5vrhSvqNKXX1qRtaMgHwzk92-Dj_Q3W8FOkPzNf2gSlXRzYr7SMKMJmcSH1Lc-EuxeIknff2bNI-M_8QJ_ooUS2OR7JOfkyckBzPS2wHDBRo4PFRWxduEZgKlMcdpEVnGmNHfkWSDmnF7DEPNi_L0qJ9WCLjEvGMsNMRkBpvgblCtZ7axsdsUIx1cXlPJjwDMP6l3guU4uNtWYTWi4MlXRYi9Yby2C29W6rMwY81mx3HybwGvve-GdSfZ17gqowh_s0A_sX2kshsJIudJ1T1QoP_U3YIBvNn4t_LG_no1BwfQd5NS4T54ds9boqb8PX3x0wv6BOF_z93R5PMCdlheIBHxUg53DJsXvoaDv2bh1eQONl_BYUAxEV1g2FFeknV6s2JrGv3HOH3_VY38JM06tL2SUz3Wiv6OXznhexqJkokNlHGOpPpid3sfJkXHsIyLVk-PDJSZi9kKr5bBOb5THosjRXYBaK7gQaDKDqZV5FDpKtca_zwsHhdmtDWDVC-6N2hQ7kqztug6tOAhuOmoqXHG_LDH0PXaK66FSieLMiiqctNuS2Q%3D)**

I am ready to continue his legacy. | Fellow Patriot, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult few weeks. I intend to earn every vote because that's what this job demands, and that's what South Carolina deserves. name: Team Hong
subject: A moderate, centerist Democrat
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
He's all-in on Fran
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260726-3080)
Peter,
Happy Sunday!
Every week, we share a story from someone who's part of this movement. Today’s testimonial comes from Menomonie Mayor Matthew Crowe, who leads a city in Dunn County, which Donald Trump carried by 16 points in 2024.
Crowe describes himself as a moderate, centrist Democrat. By his own account, he's not the kind of elected official you'd expect to endorse a democratic socialist for governor.
But he’s all in for Fran. Here's why, in his words:
* * *
_"For too long, the people of the diminishing middle class have been fighting a rigged system. Our hard earned tax dollars end up subsidizing the ultra rich while they pay the lowest tax percentages. Our public schools, childcare, healthcare and rural communities go underfunded, while corporate welfare and tax breaks go to those who do not need it and only get richer from it. Something drastic has to change._
_As a moderate/centrist Democrat, I usually wouldn't endorse a democratic socialist. However, Francesca doesn't want to give free handouts. She wants to give all Wisconsinites a fair chance at a fair game with making housing, childcare and healthcare more affordable. Francesca will also invest in growing middle class jobs and development for us all and not just big tech and data centers as we see from this federal administration._
_As a mayor of a city in Wisconsin, I am excited to see Francesca lead the charge in bringing local control back to the cities, fix our shared revenue system and allow cities to operate as they seem fit without state government overreach."_
**— Mayor Matthew Crowe, Menomonie**
* * *
He’s not alone. This week, 27 local elected officials and community leaders across 13 counties [endorsed Fran for governor](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16897?t=1&akid=3080%2E105371%2E5iNCEz). A few of their words:
_"People are tired of hate and division. They want a governor with a backbone, someone who will deliver permanent affordability and stand up for every single one of us. I'm a fan of Fran."_
**— Supervisor Melissa Custer, Ozaukee County**
_"Wisconsin needs Francesca Hong in the Governor's office. She’s someone who knows how to work hard, solve problems, and never back down from a fight. As the child of first-generation immigrants, Fran has had to earn every opportunity through determination and grit. That same fighting spirit is exactly what Wisconsin needs today."_
**— Huma Ahsan, attorney, Dane County**
_"Everywhere I go, I meet enthusiastic supporters who are inspired by her vision for Wisconsin. Fran has always fought for working families, championing affordable healthcare, strong public schools, paid leave, universal childcare, and free school meals for every child."_
**— Supervisor Rodolfo Abarca, Rock County**
_"If we dream of a new way of life for Wisconsin, then we must elect someone who is brave enough to lead beyond the Democratic establishment norms. Francesca is that person."_
**— Karen Mischel, former Mayor of Viroqua**
The [full list](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16897?t=2&akid=3080%2E105371%2E5iNCEz) of endorsers spans city councils, county boards, school boards, and village halls in Brown, Dane, Dunn, Eau Claire, La Crosse, Marathon, Outagamie, Ozaukee, Portage, Richland, Rock, Trempealeau, and Vernon counties.

* * *
Local leaders know what’s at stake with this election, and they know what their communities need. When they say Fran is the candidate who will actually deliver for Wisconsin, it's because they've read our plans and because they've seen her show up.
Movements like this one aren't funded by lobbyists or corporate PACs. They're funded by people like you.
**[We’re just over two weeks from the primary. Please consider making a donation today: Every dollar we raise keeps organizers on doors, from Menomonie to Madison.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260726.yru6Jf&refcode=em20260726-3080&t=3&akid=3080%2E105371%2E5iNCEz)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260726.yru6Jf&amount=5&refcode=em20260726-3080&t=6&akid=3080%2E105371%2E5iNCEz)**
With gratitude,
Team Hong
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260726-3080&t=7&refcode2=3080_105371_5iNCEz&akid=3080%2E105371%2E5iNCEz)**

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
I’m committed to doing everything I can to stand up for Californians and keep holding the lawless, chaotic, and cruel Trump administration accountable.
That’s why I’ve sued Trump *more than once a week* since he returned to office last January. That’s the pace at which he is brazenly, repeatedly breaking the law and violating the Constitution.
I will never apologize for holding the most powerful man in the country accountable when he oversteps the bounds of his power. He might not like it, but the truth is, his power isn’t limitless. He isn’t a king.
But Trump continues to target California. Our healthcare. Our schools. Our public safety. Our immigrant communities. None of us can sit back while the federal government attacks our rights, our neighbors, and our values, and we’ve got a long way to go until Trump finally leaves office.
That's one reason why I'm running for re-election this November — California needs an Attorney General ready to keep fighting. Today, we’re exactly 100 days away from Election Day, and the stakes are only getting higher.

**by Brett Di Resta (**_**with contributions by Cliff Schecter**_**)**
The event-horizon-like implosion of Graham Platner in Maine calls into question everything I thought I knew about Democratic strategists and research.
As many must know by now, Daniel Moraff of the political consulting firm _The Fight Agency_ "discovered" Graham Platner and immediately fell in love. And not just a quotidian kind of love. The love of fairy tales and Trump family pre-nups. Moraff had Platner pegged as our next President before he even had the nomination to run as the Democratic Senate candidate from Maine.
Which perhaps blinded him to the obvious.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a06b7775-ef2f-4a62-99d6-4bab64e35b52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Rather than taking their time and do it right, the consultants paid a research firm $6,250 and gave them just _three days_ to vet Platner's background. Additionally, Moraff (who has his own, personal vetting issues) copped in an interview to immediately tossing aside all of the research findings he had rushed to receive for pennies on the dollar.
Trust me when I tell you _that the initial vet of someone planning to run for the U.S. Senate should take several weeks, and cost at least twice as much as what Moraff paid_. Watching him brag about his incompetent vetting strategy is like seeing someone buy gas station sushi--then boast about getting it on the cheap while ambling toward an outhouse.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5849f600-0bd8-4599-8017-293483c9f9bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There is an old adage that Washington, D.C. is just Hollywood for ugly people. Comedian Jay Leno, former host of _The Tonight Show_ , was fond of repeating that one to the oft-uproarious laughter of his late-show audience.
And if it's true for Democratic consultants--political researchers are most certainly dead last on the call sheet. But when they need us, _they_ _need us_. That's why after 30 years as an opposition researcher, I'm at peace with our place in the campaign firmament. I take comfort in the fact that the true political ball-knowers--the professionals who take their jobs seriously and want to win their campaigns--greatly value what we do.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5e021af8-31e7-4583-aa49-353e904482de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_**Or at least, they used to**_. Moraff--obviously--but also too many among his ilk seem to neither understand nor value the contribution and/or necessity of quality opposition research.
In fact, it is where too many campaigns--Democratic ones we care about--truly get it wrong these days.
The problem was not simply that vulnerabilities existed--it was that no one seemed to understand what professional vetting was actually supposed to accomplish. So let me tell you exactly where these campaigns failed, why they keep making the same mistakes over-and-over again, and how competent campaigns handle these situations **before** they become front-page news.
What _**should**_ they have done? Let's start with Platner and go through the list. Yes, sadly, **there 's a list of Democratic debacles this campaign cycle that are threatening the kind of wave election we should have**--by every metric available.
**Ok, let 's get started.**
**Cliff 's Note:**
This rest is for [paid subscribers](https://substack.com/redirect/5e021af8-31e7-4583-aa49-353e904482de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) because we're not just building a newsletter--_we 're giving you access_ to expertise usually reserved for presidents & party chiefs.
Brett Di Resta is known as one of **the best**. He has shaped elections that have changed the world. Campaigns pay handsomely for his insights.
They're not on cable news. Or TikTok. 3,000+ of you pay just a latte per month **to get them here**. **For the truth** _**behind**_**the curtain**. **If you 're a free subscriber, come on in--[become a paid subscriber](https://substack.com/redirect/5e021af8-31e7-4583-aa49-353e904482de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), see what you're missing.**

**I’m not what you’d call a “typical” politician. **
Back in the mid-1980s, I was a geologist — until I wasn’t. Our company got sold, and we all got laid off. I used part of my severance to buy an old Chevy convertible, and drove to visit my brother in Berkeley, CA. He showed me one of the first brewpubs in America, and I loved it. I came back to Denver and took a gamble, risking every scrap of my savings in opening the Wynkoop Brewing Company in downtown Denver.
I remember working 80-hour weeks. I remember lying awake at night, wondering how we were going to make it. And I remember being so frustrated that our government was focusing on decisions that’d help politicians get reelected rather than helping solve our problems.
All of this is to say: I never planned to run for public office, let alone the U.S. Senate. But to tell you the truth, I was fed up with everyday Coloradans’ voices being drowned out by corporate interests and the wealthy.
So I ran for Mayor. To everyone’s surprise, especially mine, I won in a landslide. From then on, I focused every day on making decisions based on what was best for Denver.
I then became the first Denver Mayor in 120 years to be elected Governor, on the premise of uniting people and getting things done. We expanded health care to half a million people and created the first methane regulations in any state or country in the world.
And after we flipped Colorado’s Senate seat in 2020, we worked to deliver real change for Coloradans. We invested billions of dollars to confront the climate crisis, lowered prescription drug costs, made investments to rebuild our infrastructure, and brought thousands of good-paying manufacturing jobs back to America.
Now, we’re in the fight of our lives as Trump’s extreme agenda threatens to undo all that work. We refused to let him auction off our public lands or use your tax dollars to give handouts to felons like Tina Peters.
Some of our most important fights are ahead of us, and we’ll need to retake the Senate if we’re going to do it.
**This won’t be an easy path forward. MAGA has been looking for any opportunity to flip Colorado red again and tighten their grip on DC. It’s going to take all of us to fend them off and hold the line for Democrats. That’s why we’re coming to you:**

You are invited to join our one-click issue response poll.

Alleged non-citizen voting has been a talking point since the 2024 elections.
However, the nonpartisan Center for Election Innovation & Research spent much of 2025 tracking state governments and their efforts across the country, and has confirmed that non-citizen voting is extremely rare and non-coordinated.
In fact, Louisiana's Republican Secretary of State Nancy Landry recently announced that a grand total of 79 possible non-citizens had voted in the state over the last 40 years. The nonpartisan Brennan Center for Justice estimates that more than 74 million votes were cast in Louisiana over that time period, making this approximately 1 out of every 1 million votes cast.
Secretary of State Landry also acknowledged that she couldn’t even be sure that those 79 were actual cases of ineligible votes being cast — some may have been incorrectly identified as a result of data errors or outdated information.
We want to hear from voters in your area about this topic. Will you take our one-question poll right away?

That’s a problem in any campaign. But in a battleground state as competitive and expensive as Pennsylvania, it’s especially risky.
**_We still need to reach undecided voters._**
**_We still need to respond to attacks._**
**_We still need to organize across all 67 counties._**
**_And we still need to make sure Pennsylvanians hear the truth before outside groups flood the airwaves with lies._**
The truth is, this team already knows what Josh stands for.

They're happening in quiet, under-the-radar races that most people never hear about, and that's exactly where Big Polluters want to keep them. That’s why today I want to shine a spotlight on two critical races in Washington State. I'm proud to announce that JanePAC is endorsing Vanessa Kritzer (LD-45) and Renee Hernandez Greenfield (LD-26) for Washington State House. = = Now, let me introduce you to these two remarkable climate leaders: | 🗳️ Vanessa Kritzer (State House, LD-45, Pos. 2) is running for a seat JanePAC knows well — we backed a climate champion here in 2024 against the 10-term moderate incumbent. Now that incumbent has retired, the seat is wide open, and this time we have an experienced, trusted climate leader ready to claim it: a nearly seven-year city council veteran and Council President who has helped to protect thousands of acres of forest and increase access to trails and parks for everyone. She has also delivered a strategy to achieve net zero for carbon emissions, salmon habitat restoration, and clean energy programs for working families. 🗳️ Renee Hernandez Greenfield (State House, LD-26, Pos. 2) is running in one of Washington's true swing districts: an open seat where the outgoing Republican won by 9 points in 2024. Flipping it won't be easy, and it starts with advancing through this primary. Renee’s climate leadership is rooted in the communities that absorb environmental harm first: Indigenous families whose livelihoods depend on a healthy Puget Sound and low-income children living closest to industrial polluters. The GOP stockpiled a lot of money in anticipation.
|

Peter – we’re about to ask you to [**_chip in your first donation of $5 to Roy Cooper’s Senate campaign today,_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk848&amounts=5%2C25%2C50%2C100%2C250&amount=5&t=8&akid=2303%2E124072%2EWKcvO9) and there’s a critical reason why:
The Supreme Court recently made a game-changing decision that directly impacts the upcoming midterm elections – the most impactful campaign finance decision since Citizens United.
**The far-right majority decided to give billionaires and shady corporate PACs unlimited power to drown out the voices of millions of voters and small-dollar donors everywhere.**
In anticipation of this ruling, the Republican Party stockpiled _a lot_ of money. A $600 million edge over Democrats, to be precise.
_Why?_
Because they knew they’d have to bail out their lackluster Senate candidates, like our opponent, former RNC Chair Michael Whatley, to save their chances of holding the majority.
**That’s the reason Roy set a goal for us to raise $1.5 million by the July end-of-month deadline. It’s the only way we’ll be able to fight back against the GOP’s well-funded attacks and win this race – which experts are saying will be the priciest Senate race of all time.**
[**_We know it seems daunting, but your contribution of $5 now, or even just a few bucks, will truly go a long way toward helping us flip North Carolina – and with it, the Senate majority. So please, Peter, can we count on you?

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5676501c-4bf7-408e-87fc-a0c37635083d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As many of you are aware, I run a frozen pizza factory. Pepperoni pizza is one of our best sellers, so it should not be surprising that I spend a lot of time thinking about pork prices. And while the price of your pizza is obviously impacted by the price of pepperoni on top of it, you may find it interesting that the price is increasingly being set in Beijing, not in Iowa or North Carolina.
How's that? Well, it turns out that the Middle Kingdom is the world's largest consumer of pork. China consumes [57 million metric tons of pork per year](https://substack.com/redirect/aeae54eb-6e59-471e-ae22-6752cab84808?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--roughly **half of all the pork eaten on Earth**. And pork in China isn't like chicken in America. The Chinese character for "home" (家) is literally a pig under a roof and pork is deeply intertwined with Chinese culture. So when anything disrupts China's pork supply (such as a disease, tariff, or trade war), shockwaves flow through global markets. Including, eventually, to the pepperoni we put on pizzas in America.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/7d86adb1-c66a-4b31-8862-eb1ee2f33e5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But there's an interesting twist to the story that very few people talk about. China doesn't just buy American pork chops and tenderloins. [It buys the parts of the pig that Americans won't touch](https://substack.com/redirect/2c1a1e86-2965-459f-90ba-d3d784330968?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): the feet, the heads, the stomachs, the ears, the hearts. China takes [59% of all US pork "variety meat" exports](https://substack.com/redirect/08a1f64b-4b85-424e-a7d3-b600d1d53d3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The National Pork Producers Council puts it bluntly: ["There is no alternative market"](https://substack.com/redirect/08a1f64b-4b85-424e-a7d3-b600d1d53d3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that can absorb this volume.
Why does this matter for pepperoni? Because the revenue from selling those pig feet to China **subsidizes the cost of the rest of the pig**. Every part of the animal that gets sold offshore reduces the effective cost of the trim that stays here--the trim that gets cured, fermented, and turned into pepperoni. When China stops buying feet, that revenue vanishes, and the cost of producing the cuts Americans _do_ eat goes up. Pig feet you've never thought of and will probably never eat quietly keep your favorite pizza affordable.
* * *
## [Pepperoni Pizza Politics](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0f75c9-6c88-4049-93ac-076b52d96ae2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| August 25, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0f75c9-6c88-4049-93ac-076b52d96ae2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[As an academic, author, consultant, entrepreneur, and corporate board member, I have long understood that federal regulations and government overreach were burdening businesses, but as the CEO of a food manufacturing business, I have a specific example worth highlighting.](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0f75c9-6c88-4049-93ac-076b52d96ae2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/fc0f75c9-6c88-4049-93ac-076b52d96ae2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
And of course the buying slows to a trickle whenever the trade war heats up. Over the past several years, [US pork tariffs in China have swung from 12% to 81%](https://substack.com/redirect/74e90cb9-2d37-4d0b-9636-644437555022?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). At 81%, trade effectively stops. The [November 2025 deal](https://substack.com/redirect/434b1135-700a-4d09-b8df-f9aa5857ed82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) brought tariffs down and granted waivers on the worst duties, but those waivers expire at the end of 2026. The pork industry received a reprieve, not a resolution.
But these dynamics, we must remember, work in two directions. When China _needs_ pork, it doesn't just buy, it hoovers up whatever it can find. In 2018, [African Swine Fever killed roughly half of China's pig herd](https://substack.com/redirect/b8fb3954-afbd-42a7-91e2-646624cbe8cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), hundreds of millions of animals. Chinese pork prices spiked **46.7% in a single year**. China bought everything it could find on the global market, pulling supply away from processors everywhere, including the ones making pepperoni for American pizza companies. They also made massive investments into their domestic pork industry, including the now infamous "pig skyscrapers."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/24c25572-ee3f-4d02-9df4-e04169e3b26e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Separately, there's also a twist steeped in international intrigue. [Smithfield Foods](https://substack.com/redirect/07a5ed89-4eb8-44f2-91b5-d60c1a019622?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (America's largest pork producer, responsible for **23% of the entire US pork market**) is owned by China's WH Group. The Chinese company bought it for $4.7 billion in 2013.
I remember speaking with Congressional leaders then and many were concerned about the impact the acquisition might have on food safety. Many were concerned that Chinese food safety standards would transform the US food company and put our hot dogs or bacon at risk. I remember discussing it with Smithfield executives at the time who were confused by this suggestion, and correctly (it turns out) noted that the Chinese were seeking to learn US food safety procedures so they could take them to China.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e965973c-65a0-41e3-9fa2-8c6501cc70fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nevertheless, the concern about Chinese ownership of US agriculture and food assets has not dissipated. In 2023, for instance, [Virginia passed a law](https://substack.com/redirect/e63965bb-39d6-449c-a38a-8bd9a48ebdcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) banning "foreign adversaries" from owning farmland in the state. Well, it turns out that Smithfield has farms in Virginia. One national security critic [put the concern simply](https://substack.com/redirect/e63965bb-39d6-449c-a38a-8bd9a48ebdcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "If we get into some sort of world disaster, where do you think China's going to send their pork? They're going to send it back to China." Who would have thought that pepperoni could be a national security issue?
These dynamics are a useful reminder that something as simple as pizza is an amalgamation of countless supply chains, geopolitical dynamics, disease, weather, and politics. Even small events happening on the other side of the globe can ripple through the economy and impact the price of frozen pizza. Connecting these seemingly unrelated dots can help us understand the levers that impact prices and drive supply. The geoeconomics of the pork industry may seem large and lofty and irrelevant to most, but can, via the price of pepperoni, impact the price of your pizza.
The price of pepperoni was shaped by a tariff negotiated in Geneva, a pig disease that started in a province most Americans can't pronounce, an acquisition that handed a quarter of America's pork supply to a Chinese conglomerate, and 59% of the pig (parts no one here will eat) being shipped across the Pacific. Think about that next time you take a bite of a slice!

clean_body: Every fellow receives a stipend thanks to supporters like you. | | | | People frequently ask me what gives me hope for the future, and even during some of the darkest moments in our country, I can list a number of things that give me hope. But at the top of the list, my hope and inspiration consistently come from one group: young people. Early on in my campaign, I decided that I wanted to create a space for young people to learn, grow, and realize that their talent and brilliance could change the world. My team and I created the Frontera Fellows program to offer paid summer internships for El Paso high school and college students. These young people are incredible, and we are honored to have them working with us and learning the ins and outs of campaign strategy, legislative advocacy, and community organizing while gaining firsthand experience in public service. Meet this year's class: = These bright young leaders remind me every day that the future of El Paso is in good hands. Most young El Pasoans need to work and don't have the luxury of participating in volunteer programs, so our fellowship ensures every participant receives a $600 stipend. I never want a student's financial circumstances to stand in the way of this opportunity. That stipend comes directly from campaign funds, and I raise money specifically for this program. = = Thank you for helping ensure these young El Pasoans can earn while they learn — and for investing in the future of our community. With gratitude, Veronica | Donate Today If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Veronica Escobar instantly: | = | = | = | = ---|---|---|--- | | | Paid for by Veronica Escobar for Congress. |
